why: Every Levels pick starts level one. The index is carried through three layers -- HUD callback, start request, start boundary -- and this is the join where losing it produces a working game on the wrong board rather than an error. 1 of 25 -- 'a Levels pick asks for that level, carrying the index', which drives index 3 specifically. A fixture that happened to pick level 0 could not see this, which is why that case does not.
